I also want to say this - 2026 has legitimately been a hard year. We’ve had multiple sharp rotations, violent pullbacks, failed breakouts, and periods where the market went from rewarding risk to punishing it very quickly.

My portfolio itself had a -13.7% month in March and a -25.9% month in July. So seeing +102.67% YTD today means a lot more to me than just the number.

No options. No penny stocks. No chasing every theme that gets hot. Just shares.

Finding businesses where I believe the fundamentals are getting stronger, using technicals to figure out when I want to get involved, sizing them based on conviction + risk, and trying to stay with my winners when the trend is working.

I’ve made plenty of mistakes this year too. Some entries could have been better. Some exits could have been better. There were times I was too early and times I could have been more aggressive.

But that’s part of the game.

The goal isn’t to build a perfect system. It’s to keep learning from every market cycle and make the framework a little better each time.

I know +100% years are not normal and I never want to start treating them like they are. My real test will be what this looks like over 5, 10, 15+ years.

Can I keep adapting? Can I survive the bad years? Can I avoid the mistakes that take me out of the game? Can I compound at a high rate for a very long time?

That matters far more to me than any single YTD number. I’m not trying to build a track record around one or two great years. I’m trying to build something that can last for decades.

Still learning. Still improving. Still hungry.

Job is not done yet.

Muse Agent 可能是下一个 ChatGPT Moment
我觉得 Muse 可能是这一轮 AI 最重要的拐点之一，有机会成为下一个 ChatGPT Moment。过去市场交易 AI，主要还是 GPU、训练和大模型能力，但 Muse 让市场第一次看到 Agent 大规模进入 C 端的可能。AI 从 Chatbot 变成 Personal Assistant，从告诉你怎么做变成直接替你做，可以帮用户处理购物、邮件、支付、客服、营销甚至跨平台任务。对 Small Business 来说，以前需要客服、运营、营销和 IT 团队完成的事情，未来可能几个 Agent 就能解决，直接降低人力和执行成本。所以 Agent的爆发点是普通人第一次能够非常直观地看到 AI 带来的 ROI，省时间，也省钱。

这也是为什么我觉得 Muse 这波不能只理解成 META 一个 APP爆了。一旦Agent Mass Adoption 开始，后面增加的是整个 AI Infrastructure 的 Token 和算力消耗，市场交易逻辑也会从单纯的 Training GPU 继续扩散到 Inference、CPU、Memory、Networking、Storage、Optical、Power 和 Data Center。AMD、ARM、MU、MRVL、COHR、LITE、AAOI和IREN、CIFR、NBIS、CRWV本质上都在交易同一件事。同时这次不只是硬件受益，Software 和应用层也会重新被定价，像Expedia、Shopify、Instacart 这些接入Agent 生态的平台，未来 AI 可以直接替用户完成订酒店、购物、买菜和支付，Agent 从流量入口进一步变成交易入口。后面我也比较期待 Apple、Google、腾讯这些拥有超级生态和海量用户的平台推出类似产品，因为他们本身就掌握设备、搜索、社交、电商或者支付入口，一旦把 Agent 真正嵌入自己的生态，AI 的 Mass Adoption 可能会进一步加速。ChatGPT 当年让所有人意识到 AI 可以和人对话，下一阶段可能是让所有人意识到，AI是真的可以替人干活、替人消费、替企业创造收入。

@Sirius_091283 Click my pinned post. I have 100s of write-ups about my processes...

This might be a long-winded writeup, so bear with me.

But leadership is more of a spectrum to me. 

I’d actually call all of those leadership, just at different points on the spectrum. 9/10 times I’m rarely trying to crown 1 stock as the official leader of a group because leadership isn’t static.

$CRWD might be the strongest leader today, $OKTA might show the strongest RS during the next market pullback, and $NET might be the first one out of a base when the group starts another leg. I care much more about identifying the basket of names where institutions are clearly putting money to work than perfectly ranking them 1-5.

When several names in the same group are acting well, I start comparing their behavior.

-which stock breaks out first?
-name closest to ATHs?
-stock refuses to go down when indices get hit?
-which one is above rising 9/21/50EMAs?
-pushes on volume and barely gives anything back?

The pullbacks usually tell me more than the rallies. So, if cybersecurity gets smoked one morning and $OKTA is sitting there down 0.5% while its peers are down 3-4%...

...guess where my eyes are going?

Weak markets reveal relative strength. That's where potential leadership becomes much easier to see.

I also care about the stock’s personality. Give me the name that trends relatively linearly, respects its MAs/pivots, tightens after expansion, and consistently gives me areas where I can define risk. Personally, I like $OKTA & $PANW the best.

A stock can technically have stronger performance than everything else in the group, but if it trades like it drank six Red Bulls every morning, it might not be the best leader for me to trade.

Leadership and tradability aren’t always the exact same thing.

Fundamentals can absolutely help explain why institutions are accumulating something, and I like knowing the story/catalyst behind a move, but fundamentals usually aren’t my tiebreaker. Price + volume are what I prioritize more than fundis. If $CRWD has the “better” fundamental story but $OKTA is showing better RS, tighter action, stronger volume characteristics + tighter risk, I’m probably trading $OKTA. I’m a trader first...I don’t need to prove which company deserves the highest valuation 5 years from now.

And I don’t necessarily need to pick only one.

If $CRWD, $OKTA, $NET and $FTNT are all repeatedly appearing on my scans, holding near highs, outperforming the market, and breaking out of quality bases, that itself is the signal. 1 strong stock can be company-specific; 4 or 5 strong stocks from the same group start looking a lot more like institutional capital rotating into the entire theme.

So my process is basically to find abnormal strength, notice which groups keep producing it, identify the handful of names leading that group, watch how they behave during weakness, and wait for MY setup in whichever leader gives me the tightest asymmetric entry.

I’m not trying to predict which cybersecurity stock will finish the year +87% versus +72%.

I’m trying to get myself into the right neighborhood, then wait for one of the nicest houses to go on sale.

Exit Liquidity ("Sell the News"):
 Institutions accumulate shares quietly before major announcements, then dump them onto retail traders who chase the euphoric headlines.

Shakeouts & False Breakouts: 
They trigger volatility on scary news to flush out stop-losses, absorb cheap shares, and instantly reverse the price.

Narrative Distraction: 
They use media hype to keep retail focused on crowded storylines while quietly positioning in true institutional leaders.

@Victory_1900 你这个逻辑是 Agent 只能把现有流量从亚马逊、Booking 手里搬走。

我想的是Agent 如果把搜索、比价、决策、下单这些成本大幅降低，结果不只有流量重新分配，还有转化率更高、交易频率更高，把原本因为搜索成本、决策成本、操作成本太高被压抑的需求释放出来。比如以前订一次复杂行程，要自己查航班、酒店、路线、价格，很多人嫌麻烦就不做了。如果 Agent 几分钟直接给方案并完成预订，交易发生的概率就会上升。这里增加的是需求转化率、交易频率和可被服务的场景。未来还有很多类似场景的应用，所以蛋糕是有可能变大的。

至于算力投入，这确实是前期成本，但互联网、云计算早期也都是先重投入，再靠规模化把单位成本打下来。最后要看的是每一美元推理成本最终能创造多少新增交易和收入。

现在交易的是整个 Agent 时代的想象空间。资本市场已经在用脚投票，如果Agent 成为下一代入口，背后带动的不只是C端软件应用层，还会继续拉动云、算力、存储、网络和数据中心需求，这里面的资本想象力和炒作空间都很大。

1 of the strangest challenges I’ve had as my account has grown is learning that the %'s can stay exactly the same while the emotions completely change.

Losing 1-3% when that dollar amount represents a nice steak dinner feels very different from losing the same 1-3% when my brain starts translating the number into a car, a year of rent, or something else tangible.

Mathematically, nothing changed, but psychologically, EVERYTHING did.

I’ve caught myself hesitating on perfectly valid entries simply because I knew what the loss would look like in $$'s. I’ve tightened stops that had absolutely no business being tightened because watching the P&L fluctuate made me uncomfortable.

And probably the most expensive one, I’ve taken profits WAY too early because a large $$ gain felt too good to risk giving back. The irony is that trying so hard to protect myself from a larger dollar loss can actually destroy the exact process that grew the account in the first place.

I'm choking my process if I move my stops before getting first trims or a decent cushion.

If my system says the trade is invalid below LOD, but I randomly move my stop higher because I’m down an uncomfortable dollar amount, I’m no longer trading my system. I’m strictly trading my P&L. Normal volatility knocks me out, the stock turns around without me, and suddenly I’m staring at the screen wondering why I didn’t just follow the frickin' plan.

The same thing happens with winners.

A +$2,000 open gain might have once felt incredible...later, that same percentage move could represent +$20,000.

My instinct naturally wants to grab it because $20k is REAL money. But if I constantly convert every fluctuation into what I could buy with it, I’ll never give an exceptional position enough room to become an exceptional winner. The larger my account gets, the more I have to think in percentages, Rmultiples + process instead of $$'s.

That’s something I’m still actively working through, and I don’t pretend I’ve mastered it. I will likely never master this concept because I'm human.

My solution has increasingly been to define the risk BEFORE entering, size the position so I can genuinely tolerate that loss, and then stop renegotiating with myself once money is moving around. If the planned dollar loss makes me uncomfortable enough that I know I’ll interfere with the trade, I’m simply too big.

And will take that as a precaution to size down a bit.

Growing an account doesn’t magically eliminate trading psychology...if anything, it can actually expose an entirely new layer of it.

The numbers get bigger, but my job stays stupidly simple:

1) know my entry,
2) know my invalidation,
3) accept the risk before clicking buy...
...and then give the trade enough room to do what I originally bought it to do.

The goal isn’t becoming numb to money; it’s making sure the money doesn’t change my process!

Just my 2 cents I'm currently working through.

Godspeed, family!

Even if I share my entire process, all my rules, my market view every night and every morning in live sessions, and every trade in real time with exact entries, trims, exits, and position sizing, I can still say with a lot of confidence that only a small number of people will really internalize it well enough to become consistently good at it, and even fewer will eventually surpass me. That has very little to do with access to information and almost everything to do with what happens when the process gets uncomfortable.

When the market is clean and trades are working, everybody believes in the system. The real test comes when you get chopped up, go through a drawdown, miss a few moves, or hit one of those stretches where nothing seems to cooperate. And yes, that happens to real traders too. That’s usually when most people start questioning everything at once. They assume the system stopped working, jump to another style, start changing rules in the middle of the game, or sometimes stop trading altogether.

That’s also why I think there’s a huge difference between simply following trades and actually learning how to trade. Copying an entry is easy. Understanding why the trade was taken, why the size was chosen, why something was trimmed, why exposure was reduced, and why you sometimes have to keep doing the same thing through a rough stretch is much harder.

A big part of what I try to do inside PrimeTrading is make that whole decision-making process visible. The live trades matter, but the real value is seeing the thinking behind them over and over again, especially during the difficult periods. That’s where people either build conviction in a process or keep jumping from one answer to the next.

And in the end, that’s probably the biggest separator of all.
